name: Gawri

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Gawri (kala1373).

notes: Gawri (Kalam Kohistani), a Dardic Indo-Aryan language of the Swat and Dir Kohistan valleys of Pakistan, written in the Perso-Arabic orthography agreed by the Gawri spelling committee in 1995 (Baart & Sagar §2.3 'Script'), which keeps maximum conformity with Urdu and adds four letters for sounds Urdu lacks. Those four are mapped here: ݭ (Sin with two vertical nuqtas above) = ʂ, ݪ (Laam with a strike-through) = ɬ, ڄ (Bari He shape with two vertical nuqtas below) = ʈʂ, څ (Bari He shape with three nuqtas above, as in Pashto) = t̪s, plus the aspirated digraphs ڄھ ʈʂʰ and څھ t̪sʰ. Gawri has no voiced aspirates — the aspirated series in Baart & Sagar §2.1.2 Table 2 covers only the voiceless stops and affricates — so the Urdu-looking digraphs بھ دھ ڈھ گھ جھ ڑھ spell plain b d̪ ɖ ɡ dʑ ɽ. There is no glottal stop in that table either, so ع and ء are silent carriers and ئ (and the word-final sequence ئی) spells the glide j. ر is the dental flap ɾ, distinct from retroflex ڑ ɽ. Word-final ہ is the vowel a, as in Urdu. The retroflex nasal ɳ is written as the digraph نڑ, Nun plus retroflex Re (Baart & Sagar §2.3, 'The retroflex nasal'); all three gold words containing it have ɳ. The parallel digraph نگ for ŋ is an INFERENCE, not a committee-stated spelling: §2.1.2 says the phonemic status of ɳ and ŋ is not fully clear and that they might be analysed as the sequences n+ɖ and n+ɡ, and §2.3 gives a digraph only for ɳ. Four of the five gold words spelling نگ have ŋ and one (باتنگنڑ) has nasalisation plus ɡ, so the digraph is the majority reading rather than a certain one. Vowel writing follows the committee's rules (Baart & Sagar §2.3, 'The writing of Gawri vowels'): Pesh always designates u and Zer always i, so a bare Wau is the o-quality and a bare Ye the e-quality, with Jazm on either marking shortness (وْ o, یْ e); Zabar is the back open vowel a and the committee's new Zabar-with-two-dots diacritic ٞ the front open vowel æ. Because ordinary text omits the vowel diacritics, a bare Wau or Ye is scored with the committee's quality first and the alternative quality as a ranked candidate, and word-initial bare Alif is a short-vowel carrier of unrecoverable quality (long initial aː is written آ). The palatal series is written ɕ tɕ dʑ. Both sources place ⟨š č ǰ⟩ in a PALATAL column explicitly contrasted with a separate retroflex column carrying ⟨ṣ c̣⟩ (Baart & Sagar §2.1.2 Table 2; Baart 2004 §2.2 Table 2), and the alveolo-palatal sibilants are the palatal-region IPA letters, so this is a reading of the sources' own place label rather than a stated articulation. The wikipron gold's transcriber, working from Baart 1997, reads it the same way. Wikipedia's rendering of the same inventory as postalveolar ʃ tʃ dʒ flattens that place label and is not followed here. Neither tone nor vowel quality is recoverable from the scored input, and together they are the whole of this row's error. Gawri has five contrastive lexical tones (Baart & Sagar §2.2; Baart 2004 §2.3), the practical orthography leaves the tone diacritics optional and ordinary text omits them, and the wikipron gold transcribes tone on every vowel: tone marks are 348 of the 1433 NFD characters the gold's 208 rows carry under the harness's own normalisation, 24.3%. The vowel diacritics are absent outright. Exactly one of the 165 distinct gold spellings contains any of Zabar, the committee's Zabar-with-two-dots, Pesh, Zer or Jazm, and that spelling IS the bare diacritic ٞ quoted as an alphabet-table headword, so every vowel quality and every length contrast in this gold has to be guessed from an unpointed skeleton. The gold also transcribes 72 tokens of ə, a quality that is not one of the six in Baart & Sagar Table 1: it is the transcriber's symbol for exactly those unwritten short-vowel slots, and it can never be matched by a spec that emits the six-vowel inventory the grammar describes. Folding tone off both sides gives PER 0.2545 against 0.4170, so tone alone costs 0.1625. Folding vowels and length off as well leaves a consonant-skeleton PER of 0.0211 with 94.6% of words exact, which is where the consonant mapping above actually stands. Four gold headwords (ٞ ڄ ݪ ݭ) are alphabet-table entries glossed with the single phoneme the letter spells, and they are the row's only four exact matches. The 208 gold rows carry 165 distinct spellings; the other 43 are homograph rows differing in tone or vowel length, which the harness scores as alternative references for the same word.

wikipron.measured: Gawri has five contrastive tones (Baart & Sagar, The Gawri Language of Kalam and Dir Kohistan, SIL International, section 2.2). The 1995 spelling committee did provide tone diacritics, but section 2.3, 'The writing of tone in Gawri', states that 'on most words the tone marks would not need to be used' and that they are expected only 'in some cases ... for disambiguation'. Ordinary Gawri spelling therefore leaves tone out, and the gold bears that out exactly: 0 of the 208 rows of wikipron/gwc_arab_broad carry a tone diacritic in the Perso-Arabic column, against 204 of 208 gold transcriptions carrying one. Scored over the same 208 pairs, PER is 0.4323; folding tone out of both sides drops it to 0.2917. Tone accounts for only about a third of this row -- the larger part of the gap is segmental and is not closed by this conclusion.

wikipron.citation: Baart & Sagar, The Gawri Language of Kalam and Dir Kohistan (https://fli-online.org/documents/languages/gawri/gawri_introduction.pdf), p. 10, 'The writing of tone in Gawri': "A set of special diacritics was made available for the writing of tone ... Although it was felt that on most words the tone marks would not need to be used, it is likely that in some cases tone marks will be necessary for disambiguation." p. 7 (2.2 Tone): "Gawri has no less than five contrastive tones." The wikipron gold transcribes tone in 204 of its 208 rows; the Perso-Arabic spelling column carries no tone diacritic. Measured by scripts/fold_gwc_notation.py with the harness's own normalize()/levenshtein() on the board's basis (165 unique words scored): as-scored PER 0.4170 (2.4% exact), matching the committed board row; with the combining acute, grave, circumflex and caron removed from BOTH sides (NFD, strip, NFC again, the form normalize() returns), 0.2626 (25.5% exact). The audit entry's 0.4323 -> 0.2917 was measured over all 208 pairs, not unique words, so the two figures differ in basis, not in finding. Vowel length is NOT folded: p. 9 says Jazm is used 'where necessary for marking shortness of a vowel', so length is partly written; tone+length folded would be 0.2526 and is not recorded. The ceiling stays above 0.25, so the row is not proved input-limited: the remaining gap is segmental.
